summary: Read-only audit of every player-facing number display in EMBERGATE's UI layer, done in response to the owner's playtest note that combat numbers read as raw engineering values ('x1.49', 'total cap is 72%', 'dodge window is 114 ms') rather than legible RPG stats. This document is the SPEC ONLY — no src/ files were changed. It (1) extracts how Diablo IV, Path of Exile / PoE 2, Elden Ring and World of Warcraft present the same categories of number, (2) audits ~36 concrete display sites across inventoryui.js, shopui.js, ui.js and classes.js against real current constants pulled from config.js / weapons.js / armor.js / classes.js, (3) defines one concrete conversion convention per number category with worked examples using real in-game values, and (4) splits the sites into three disjoint, file-scoped work packages so build agents do not collide. Headline finding: the three numbers the owner named by name map to three exact, fixable sites — inventoryui.js:822 and shopui.js:191 ('x1.49 power'), inventoryui.js:1246 ('total capped 72%' with no total ever shown), and inventoryui.js:1235 ('114 ms' with no scale). A fourth, less obvious finding: the EQUIPPED weapon readout's own 'Power' row is generated by weaponSummary() in src/game/weapons.js — a file NOT in the build agents' owned-file list — so Package B must intercept/replace that specific row inside inventoryui.js rather than edit weapons.js.

conventions: Weapon damage on the item itself is a flat range/number (base weapon damage), not a multiplier or percentage.

Bonus damage sources use an explicit notation to separate stacking rules: '[x]' prefixes MULTIPLICATIVE percent bonuses, '[+]' prefixes ADDITIVE percent bonuses. Neither is ever shown as a bare 'x1.49' with no sign or label — the bracket glyph is the label.
Chance-based combat stats (Critical Strike Chance, etc.) are shown as plain percentages on the character sheet.
Some effects (Thorns, certain legendary procs) are flat numbers with no percent at all when there is no natural baseline to scale.

conventions: Weapon damage is shown as a flat min-max range on the weapon tooltip; DPS is a separately computed, separately labelled number, never conflated with the raw range.

Chance-based stats (Critical Strike Chance, Evasion-derived dodge chance) are percentages on the character sheet and on skill tooltips — confirms the genre keeps chance stats as %, which this codebase should NOT 'fix'.

PoE's own evasion/dodge system is itself an internally complex roll (entropy-smoothed chance-to-be-hit) that the game nonetheless always surfaces to the player as a single percentage, never as the underlying formula terms.

conventions: Attack Rating (AR) — the game's single headline damage number — is ALWAYS a flat integer, never a multiplier and never a percentage. It is explicitly the sum of two flat components shown side by side: base weapon damage + stat-scaling bonus damage (e.g. '221 + 97').

This is the strongest precedent in the research set for EMBERGATE's specific ask: a weapon's power is communicated to the player as one flat, addable number, with the formula's inputs visible, not as a raw coefficient.

citations.title: How to interpret weapon stats and character status in Elden Ring

conventions: Item TOOLTIPS show combat stats as raw 'rating' points (an internal currency), which is why third-party addons exist specifically to convert rating into a percentage — stock WoW tooltips are, if anything, LESS legible than a bare multiplier for this one case.

The CHARACTER PANE (the sheet, not the item tooltip) shows the final, already-converted percentages for Crit/Haste/etc. — the same split EMBERGATE already has: raw rolled values on armor pieces (stash comparison) vs. final derived percentages on the STATS tab. This validates keeping the STATS tab's existing '%' presentation and focusing fixes on the RAW multiplier and RAW millisecond leaks into player-facing rows.

Cast times / channel times — WoW's closest analogue to a millisecond-scale timing window — are always shown in whole or half seconds ('1.5 sec cast'), never in milliseconds. No researched game surfaces a player-facing stat in raw milliseconds; this is the basis for the seconds-conversion rule below, by analogy rather than direct precedent, since none of the four games has a directly equivalent 'perfect-dodge window' stat exposed as a number at all (Elden Ring's own i-frames are undocumented in-game and only exist in community datamines).

R1_flatDamageFromMultiplier.rule: Any place currently printing a bare weapon multiplier ('x1.49', 'x1.30 power') next to a rarity/name gets replaced with a computed FLAT per-hit damage number, derived from the exact formula already shipped in weapons.js: hitDamage(w, step, atk) = atk * w.dmgMul * step.dmg (weapons.js:2234).
R1_flatDamageFromMultiplier.representativeStep: Use w.combo[0] — the weapon's OPENING hit — as the representative combo step. Justification: (a) every archetype's combo array has one, so the choice is uniform across all 8 families; (b) it is the swing the player experiences most often and first; (c) it matches the Elden Ring / WoW precedent of showing a single per-swing/per-hit number rather than a full-combo total or an averaged DPS figure, which would need new derived state this wave is not scoped to add. Flagged as an interpretive design call in openQuestions — an 'average across combo steps' is the documented alternative.
R1_flatDamageFromMultiplier.atkSource: Use the CURRENT WIELDER's live attack power, `game.derived.atk` (already computed by game.refreshDerived and already read this way by ui.js's pause card at ui.js:213) — never a recomputed or assumed value. This makes the shown number answer the exact question a player has when comparing gear: 'what would this weapon do for ME right now.' shopui.js does not currently import config.js/classes.js at all; it only needs `this.game.derived.atk`, which is already on the live Game instance it holds.
R1_flatDamageFromMultiplier.roundingAndLabel: Round to the nearest whole number, suffix 'dmg/hit' (not 'power', not 'dmg' alone — 'power' is exactly the abstract word the owner is asking to be replaced by something concrete). Keep the existing `·` separator grammar and row position — this is a text-node swap inside an existing `small`/`meta` node, not a new row.

R2_bareMultiplierToPercent.rule: Any bare 'xN.NN' multiplier on a STAT (not a weapon) with no natural flat baseline — critDmg, skillMul, shadowDmgMul, knockTakenMul, and the CLASS_QUALITY multiplier — converts to signed percent-bonus language: `${sign}${Math.round((v - 1) * 100)}%`. This matches Diablo IV's own convention of never showing a bare coefficient, always a signed percent with an explicit polarity.
R2_bareMultiplierToPercent.specialCase_knockTakenMul: This field is 'damage taken', so LOWER is BETTER — the sign must read naturally either direction: 0.85 → '-15% knockback taken' (good), 1.40 → '+40% knockback taken' (bad). Do not flip the sign to force it positive; the existing colour convention elsewhere in the panel (green=good/red=bad) already carries the valence, the text should just be honest about direction.
worked: critDmg: d.critDmg = 1.5 + agi*0.0035 (config.js:366). A fresh level-1 hunter (agi 0): critDmg = 1.50 → today's row reads 'x1.50'; new row reads '+50%'. At agi 40 (spent+auto): critDmg = 1.64 → '+64%'.
skillMul: d.skillMul = 1 + intel*0.025 (config.js:370). At intel 20 (spent+auto): skillMul = 1.50 → today 'x1.50'; new '+50% skill damage'.
shadowDmgMul: d.shadowDmgMul = (1 + intel*0.011) * armorMul (config.js:390). At intel 20, no armour bonus: 1.22 → today 'x1.22'; new '+22% shadow damage'.

CLASS_QUALITY (classes.js:148): base=1.00, advanced=1.12, sovereign=1.25 → today's CLASS block prints 'quality advanced x1.12'; new prints 'ADVANCED · +12% to class benefits' (base quality shows '+0%', i.e. still visible, not hidden, so a base-tier player can see there is headroom).

R3_chancePercentagesStayPercentages.rule: Crit chance, dodge/crit-chance-adjacent stats, damage reduction, cooldown reduction, and attack speed STAY percentages — confirmed by all four researched games (WoW's character-pane %, Diablo/PoE's crit-chance %, PoE's evasion-derived dodge %). Do not convert these to anything else. The only change is FORMAT consistency: no trailing '.0' unless the value itself is sub-1%.
R3_chancePercentagesStayPercentages.formatFunction: fmtPct(v): let p = v*100; if (Math.abs(p) < 1 && p !== 0) return `${p.toFixed(1)}%`; else return `${Math.round(p)}%`. This replaces inventoryui.js's existing `pct()` helper (line 388, currently always `.toFixed(1)`, which is why '55.0%' and '60.0%' currently appear) and needs a local twin in ui.js (which does not import from inventoryui.js and has its own inline `${(d.crit*100).toFixed(1)}%` at ui.js:244).
R3_chancePercentagesStayPercentages.capWording: Every 'cap' gets the value it is a cap OF, printed in the SAME grammar already used by the STATS tab's own row() sub-label (its 3rd argument) for Crit chance / Attack speed / Cooldown cut / Damage reduction — e.g. row('Crit chance', pct(d.crit), `cap ${pct(cap)}`) already exists at inventoryui.js:1225-1230. This is the concrete, justified choice for the 'total cap is 72%' fix: reuse that exact established sub-label slot rather than invent a new visual (a mini bar), because it is zero new UI surface and the player has already learned to read it three rows above. See R5 for the specific 72% fix.

R4_millisecondsToSeconds.rule: dodgeWindow and tellLeadMs (and their class-text equivalents) convert from raw milliseconds to seconds at 2 decimals, PLUS the value's own known ceiling from config.js, printed via the same row() sub-label pattern as R3's caps.
worked: Dodge window (inventoryui.js:1235, the exact site the owner cited): d.dodgeWindow is already stored in SECONDS internally (config.js:388 divides by 1000) but the UI re-multiplies by 1000 to print raw ms. Fresh save (agi 0): dodgeWindow = 0.110s, cap R.agi.dodgeCapMs/1000 = 0.260s (config.js:44). Old: '110 ms'. New: row('Dodge window', '0.11s', 'cap 0.26s') — same row() call shape already used by every other capped stat in this exact block.

Enemy tell (inventoryui.js:1234): tellLeadMs base 120, cap 520 (config.js:47). Fresh save: 0.12s, cap 0.52s. Old: '120 ms — warning before a hit lands'. New: row('Enemy tell', '0.12s', 'cap 0.52s — warning before a hit lands') — keep the existing plain-language qualifier, just append it after the cap rather than replacing it.
R4_millisecondsToSeconds.deltaException: Compare-strip DELTAS (CMP_ROWS 'Tell lead' and 'Dodge window' at inventoryui.js:93 and :97, armor secondary bonuses like '+8ms') are NOT converted. A delta of '+0.01s' is LESS legible than '+8ms' — fractional-second deltas lose precision a player can act on when comparing two armor pieces. This is a deliberate, justified exception to R4: the rule targets ABSOLUTE values shown without context (which is the owner's actual complaint — '114 ms' on its own, meaning nothing), not small labelled deltas already presented as 'current → candidate (+Xms)', which are self-contextualizing.
R4_millisecondsToSeconds.classFieldLabelException: The CLASS block's base→final rows (CLASS_FIELD_LABEL, inventoryui.js:104-130, rendered at :1279 as `${base} > ${final}`) show absolute values, not deltas, so tellLeadMs and dodgeWindow DO convert here (fmtMs helper at :108 needs to switch to seconds). The '>' arrow itself in THIS numeric UI row is left alone — it is a well-established before/after stat-preview convention (WoW gear-compare tooltips, Diablo respec previews) with full units and a labelled row, which is a different thing from the bare unlabelled 'CAP 45% > 55%' inside a wall of ALL-CAPS flavour text that R6 targets.

R5_capsGetContext.rule: Every bare cap number gets the ACTUAL current value shown against it, not just the ceiling in isolation.
R5_capsGetContext.the72PercentFix: inventoryui.js:1246 currently reads: row('Armour reduction', pct(d.armorDR), 'stacks with vitality, total capped 72%') — this shows ONLY the armour layer's own percentage, then mentions a 72% ceiling that is never actually computed or shown anywhere on screen. The real combined value is `combinedDR(d.dr, d.armorDR)` from armor.js:453-455 (`Math.min(TOTAL_DR_CAP, 1 - (1-dr)*(1-armorDR))`, TOTAL_DR_CAP = 0.72 at armor.js:58) — already imported one hop away (inventoryui.js already imports from '../game/armor.js') but not currently imported into inventoryui.js. Worked example: dr 0.30 (vitality alone), armorDR 0.20 (a mid-tier set): combinedDR = 1 - (0.70 * 0.80) = 0.44. Proposed: keep the existing per-layer 'Armour reduction: 20%' row (the code's own comment at inventoryui.js:1244-1246 explains layers are shown separately ON PURPOSE so a player can see which layer moved — do not collapse that), but change its sub-label from the vague 'stacks with vitality, total capped 72%' to the concrete 'stacks with vitality — combined 44% of 72% cap', computed live every render from combinedDR(d.dr, d.armorDR).

R6_classCardText.rule: Rewrite all 16 benefitText/drawbackText strings in classes.js so none of them contain (a) 'xN.NN' notation, (b) a bare 'VALUE > VALUE' arrow with no verb — this is read BROADLY: not just percent caps ('CAP 45% > 55%') but also bare before/after arrows on raw seconds ('1.60 > 1.05S') and bare raw milliseconds ('+40MS (CAP 300MS)'), since all three are the same underlying problem (an unlabelled delta a new player cannot parse) even though the task's own example only named the percent case. Flagged in openQuestions as an interpretation the owner should confirm. Voice, ALL-CAPS, and terseness are preserved; only the confusing notations are respelled. Facts (the underlying classModifiers data) are NOT rebalanced — every rewrite below was checked against the literal benefit/drawback term set in classes.js:205-348.
